opening.quote: Good afternoon, Tidewell Home, you're speaking with Joost. How can I hell?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name, which meets the opening standard, though the sentence was garbled at the end.

verification.quote: Agent: Okay. What's the order number?
verification.comment: You asked for the order number but never confirmed the caller's full name or the postcode before reading out the delivery address, which is required before sharing account data.

understanding.quote: Customer: Hi, my lamp arrived with the shade cracked. I'm really upset, it was a birthday present.
understanding.comment: You captured the cracked-shade issue and the replacement request without asking the caller to repeat what they had already said.

resolution_accuracy.quote: A free replacement lamp is on its way and arrives in 2 to 4 working days. The was €39.95, so please send the it damaged one so back with the free return label I'm emailin you now.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The 2 to 4 working day replacement timeline and free replacement are correct, but the item is EUR 39.95 (over EUR 25), so the return label being free is correct too; the sentence is garbled but the facts stated are accurate.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: Can you email us a photo of so the cracked shade first?
process_compliance.comment: You asked for the photo before arranging the replacement, as required, and emailed the free return label, but you never asked the caller's permission before a pause in the call.

communication.quote: Customer: Hi, my lamp arrived with the shade cracked. I'm really upset, it was a birthday present.
communication.comment: When the caller said they were really upset, you did not acknowledge their distress at any point, which is a required part of good communication.

closing.quote: Agent: Thanks for calling Tidewell, goodbyes.
closing.comment: You confirmed the tracking link arrives tomorrow and asked if anything else was needed, but the close was rushed and the sign-off was unclear.
